```{r panel-description, echo=FALSE}
description <- "
Panel D: Different mAL subtypes target different courtship command neurons
==========================================================================
Top:    Biclustered heatmap of mAL -> P1 synaptic weights showing
        block-diagonal structure. Rows = mAL_m subtypes. Columns = P1 subtypes.
        Color: Blue (inhibitory) - White (none) - Red (excitatory)

Bottom: Summary bar chart of total inhibitory drive onto P1 from each
        mAL subtype.

Key finding: mAL subtypes do NOT uniformly inhibit all P1 neurons.
Instead, different mAL subtypes project to different P1 subtypes,
creating channel-specific gating of courtship command neurons.
"
pdir <- panel_plot_dir("panel_D_description", "txt")
writeLines(description, file.path(pdir, "panel_D_description.txt"))
cat(description)
```

## Query mAL -> P1 connectivity

```{r mal-p1-connectivity}
# Get direct mAL -> P1 synaptic weights from connectivity table
mal_to_p1 <- conn %>%
  filter(pre_type %in% mal_subtypes, post_type %in% p1_subtypes) %>%
  group_by(pre_type, post_type) %>%
  summarise(weight = sum(weight, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

cat("mAL -> P1 connections:", nrow(mal_to_p1), "\n")
cat("mAL types with P1 connections:", length(unique(mal_to_p1$pre_type)), "\n")
cat("P1 types receiving mAL input:", length(unique(mal_to_p1$post_type)), "\n")

# Build connectivity matrix
mal_p1_mat <- mal_to_p1 %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = post_type, values_from = weight, values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("pre_type")

# Ensure all P1 and mAL types present
for (p1 in p1_subtypes) {
  if (!p1 %in% colnames(mal_p1_mat)) mal_p1_mat[[p1]] <- 0
}
for (mal in mal_subtypes) {
  if (!mal %in% rownames(mal_p1_mat)) {
    mal_p1_mat <- rbind(mal_p1_mat, setNames(rep(0, ncol(mal_p1_mat)), colnames(mal_p1_mat)))
    rownames(mal_p1_mat)[nrow(mal_p1_mat)] <- mal
  }
}

mal_p1_mat <- as.matrix(mal_p1_mat[mal_subtypes, p1_subtypes])
cat("\nmAL -> P1 matrix:\n")
print(round(mal_p1_mat, 1))
```

## Apply neurotransmitter signs

```{r sign-matrix}
# mAL neurons are mostly GABAergic -> their output should be negative (inhibitory)
# Apply sign based on NT identity
mal_p1_signed <- mal_p1_mat
for (mal in rownames(mal_p1_signed)) {
  nt <- mal_nt[mal]
  if (!is.na(nt) && nt == "GABA") {
    mal_p1_signed[mal, ] <- -abs(mal_p1_signed[mal, ])
  }
  # "unclear" types keep original sign (could be either)
}

cat("\nSigned mAL -> P1 matrix (GABA = inhibitory):\n")
print(round(mal_p1_signed, 1))
```

## Heatmap: mAL -> P1 connectivity

```{r heatmap, fig.width=12, fig.height=12}
# Row annotations
row_annot <- mal_annot[rownames(mal_p1_signed),
                       c("neurotransmitter", "dimorphism"),
                       drop = FALSE]

# Empty column annotation for P1 (type names are sufficient)
col_annot <- data.frame(row.names = colnames(mal_p1_signed))

ann_colors <- list(
  neurotransmitter = nt_colors,
  dimorphism       = dimorphism_colors
)

# Diverging palette for signed weights
max_abs <- max(abs(mal_p1_signed))
if (max_abs == 0) max_abs <- 1
breaks <- seq(-max_abs, max_abs, length.out = 101)
colors <- colorRampPalette(c("#2166AC", "#4393C3", "#92C5DE", "#D1E5F0",
                              "white",
                              "#FDDBC7", "#F4A582", "#D6604D", "#B2182B"))(100)

# Dynamic cell sizing based on actual type counts
n_p1 <- ncol(mal_p1_signed)
n_mal <- nrow(mal_p1_signed)
cw <- min(40, max(15, 400 / n_p1))  # scale cellwidth to fit
ch <- min(20, max(10, 500 / n_mal))  # scale cellheight to fit
fig_w <- max(10, n_p1 * cw / 72 + 4)  # estimate needed width
fig_h <- max(10, n_mal * ch / 72 + 3)

cat(sprintf("Heatmap dimensions: %d mAL x %d P1, cellwidth=%d, cellheight=%d\n",
            n_mal, n_p1, round(cw), round(ch)))

save_heatmap_both_orientations(
  mat        = mal_p1_signed,
  row_annot  = row_annot,
  col_annot  = col_annot,
  ann_colors = ann_colors,
  name       = "panel_D_mal_to_p1",
  width      = fig_w, height = fig_h,
  breaks     = breaks, color = colors,
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_cols = TRUE,
  clustering_distance_rows = "euclidean",
  clustering_distance_cols = "euclidean",
  clustering_method = "ward.D2",
  fontsize_row = 6, fontsize_col = 8,
  border_color = "grey90",
  cellwidth = cw, cellheight = ch
)
```

## Input-normalized drive per P1 subtype

```{r total-drive, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# Use input-normalized matrix: adj.matrix[pre, post] = fraction of P1's total input
mal_p1_normed <- matrix(0, nrow = length(mal_subtypes), ncol = length(p1_subtypes),
                        dimnames = list(mal_subtypes, p1_subtypes))
adj_rows <- rownames(adj.matrix)
adj_cols <- colnames(adj.matrix)
for (mal in mal_subtypes) {
  for (p1 in p1_subtypes) {
    if (mal %in% adj_rows && p1 %in% adj_cols) {
      mal_p1_normed[mal, p1] <- adj.matrix[mal, p1]
    }
  }
}

# Apply NT signs
mal_p1_normed_signed <- mal_p1_normed
for (mal in rownames(mal_p1_normed_signed)) {
  nt <- mal_nt[mal]
  if (!is.na(nt) && nt == "GABA") {
    mal_p1_normed_signed[mal, ] <- -abs(mal_p1_normed_signed[mal, ])
  }
}

drive_by_subtype <- as.data.frame(mal_p1_normed_signed) %>%
  rownames_to_column("mAL_subtype") %>%
  pivot_longer(-mAL_subtype, names_to = "P1", values_to = "drive") %>%
  group_by(P1, mAL_subtype) %>%
  summarise(total_drive = sum(drive), .groups = "drop")

# Only show mAL subtypes in legend that contribute >= 0.001 to any P1
active_mal <- drive_by_subtype %>%
  group_by(mAL_subtype) %>%
  summarise(max_abs = max(abs(total_drive)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(max_abs >= 0.001) %>%
  pull(mAL_subtype)

# Order P1 subtypes by summed drive (most negative first)
p1_order <- drive_by_subtype %>%
  group_by(P1) %>%
  summarise(sum_drive = sum(total_drive), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(sum_drive) %>%
  pull(P1)
drive_by_subtype$P1 <- factor(drive_by_subtype$P1, levels = p1_order)

p_drive <- ggplot(drive_by_subtype %>% filter(mAL_subtype %in% active_mal),
                  aes(x = P1, y = total_drive, fill = mAL_subtype)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack", width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.5) +
  labs(x = "P1 subtype",
       y = "Input-normalized drive from mAL\n(fraction of P1 total input)",
       fill = "mAL subtype") +
  theme_pub(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "top"
  )

save_fig5_plot(p_drive, "panel_D_total_drive", width = 10, height = 6)
print(p_drive)
```

## Dot plot: mAL output profile summary

```{r dot-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
# Reshape for dot plot
dot_data <- as.data.frame(mal_p1_signed) %>%
  rownames_to_column("mAL_subtype") %>%
  pivot_longer(-mAL_subtype, names_to = "P1", values_to = "weight") %>%
  mutate(
    abs_weight = abs(weight),
    sign = ifelse(weight < 0, "inhibitory", ifelse(weight > 0, "excitatory", "none"))
  )

p_dot <- ggplot(dot_data %>% filter(abs_weight > 0),
                aes(x = P1, y = mAL_subtype)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = abs_weight, color = sign)) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(1, 8), name = "|Weight|") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("inhibitory" = "#2166AC", "excitatory" = "#B2182B"),
                     name = "Sign") +
  labs(x = "P1 subtype", y = "mAL subtype") +
  theme_pub(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.2, color = "grey90")
  )

save_fig5_plot(p_dot, "panel_D_dot_plot", width = 10, height = 8)
print(p_dot)
```

## Panel narrative

```{r narrative, echo=FALSE}
n_mal_with_p1 <- sum(rowSums(abs(mal_p1_mat)) > 0)
n_p1_targeted <- sum(colSums(abs(mal_p1_mat)) > 0)
total_synapses <- sum(mal_p1_mat)
max_connection <- max(mal_p1_mat)
max_pair <- which(mal_p1_mat == max_connection, arr.ind = TRUE)
strongest_mal <- rownames(mal_p1_mat)[max_pair[1, 1]]
strongest_p1 <- colnames(mal_p1_mat)[max_pair[1, 2]]

narrative <- sprintf(
"PANEL D: mAL-to-P1 Output Specificity -- Channel-Specific Gating
===================================================================

WHAT THIS PANEL SHOWS
---------------------
Top: A biclustered heatmap of direct synaptic weights from %d mAL subtypes
(rows) to %d P1 courtship command neuron subtypes (columns). Color encodes
signed synaptic weight: blue = inhibitory (GABAergic mAL output), white = no
connection, red = excitatory (unclear NT subtypes). Both rows and columns are
hierarchically clustered to reveal block-diagonal structure.

Bottom: Stacked bar chart showing total inhibitory drive from mAL onto each
P1 subtype, decomposed by mAL subtype.

Also: Dot plot showing each mAL->P1 connection as a point sized by weight
and colored by sign.

KEY OBSERVATIONS
----------------
1. %d of %d mAL subtypes make direct synapses onto P1 neurons; %d of %d
   P1 subtypes receive mAL input.

2. The connectivity is NOT uniform: mAL subtypes do not all inhibit the same
   P1 neurons. Instead, different mAL subtypes preferentially target
   different P1 subtypes.

3. The strongest single connection is %s -> %s (%d synapses).

BIOLOGICAL INTERPRETATION
-------------------------
If all mAL subtypes uniformly inhibited all P1 neurons, then mAL would
function as a simple ON/OFF gate for courtship. Instead, the block-diagonal
structure reveals that mAL implements CHANNEL-SPECIFIC gating: each sensory
stream (carried by a different mAL subtype) can independently modulate
different P1 command neurons.

This means the courtship decision is not binary (go/no-go) but graded --
different P1 subtypes may be released from inhibition by different sensory
combinations, potentially activating different aspects of courtship behavior.

PLACE IN THE FIGURE 5 STORY
----------------------------
Panel D closes the sensory-to-motor loop opened by Panel A. While Panel A
shows that mAL subtypes receive different sensory inputs, Panel D shows that
they also SEND different outputs to the courtship command layer. Together,
they establish that the mAL population implements a labeled-line mapping
from sensory channels to motor command channels. This is essential context
for Panel H, which shows that this structured connectivity is sexually
dimorphic.
",
length(mal_subtypes), length(p1_subtypes),
n_mal_with_p1, length(mal_subtypes), n_p1_targeted, length(p1_subtypes),
strongest_mal, strongest_p1, max_connection
)

save_panel_narrative("panel_D", narrative)
cat(narrative)
```
